analysis:
Integration of 16 units for the coordinator-traffic-verdict PR. It adds a read-only `Traffic:` line in status and a `coordinator traffic` check in doctor. ServingReadiness (diagnostic verdict only) and an optional `coordinator_connection` field in the daemon state file are new. UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift adds idle-gated re-registration of an unauthorized connection (15-30 min jittered, then 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h cap), supervised from ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift:82 and fed by noteCoordinatorConnection calls in ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (~299, 426, 436). Docs, tests and three log enum cases were also added.

I found no supported regression. Checks:
- T-052/T-053/A-016: the verdict is display-only. The serve path still calls clearConnectionAuthorization and cancelAppAttestShadow on each connect/disconnect, so a stale grant is not carried across connections. Re-registration reuses the existing registration flow, so it gets a fresh nonce and a fresh coordinator decision. The recovery helper grants nothing and extends no lease.
- T-057/TB-002 availability: reconnects are bounded by a 15 min threshold, per-process jitter, exponential backoff capped at 4 h and a busy gate. The coordinator is trusted, so a hostile coordinator forcing reconnects is out of scope.
- TB-012/T-059: the verdict is suppressed during an add-on hold per docs and tests. Whether the `busy` input of the recovery policy covers an active add-on hold is not visible, since ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift was not supplied. The impact would be a reconnect during a hold, which is low.
- T-058: the new state fields are a boolean, a timestamp and a counter. That is non-sensitive.

Unverified: the ServingReadiness.swift body (the integration replay omitted 84 units), the supervise/noteCoordinatorConnection implementations, the sanitization of coordinator-supplied reason strings in terminal output, and the DaemonState file permissions (pre-existing). These are recorded as open contracts rather than findings.
